date_note: 24.kg's 24 November report of the committee session gives no earlier day for the test launch.
exec: Kyrgyzstan's deputy prosecutor general says a shared system lets police pass fraud victims' account details to banks.
plain: Kyrgyzstan has started testing an anti-fraud system. Per the deputy prosecutor general, police pass victims' account details to banks, which can freeze funds for 30 days.

sources.name: 24.kg: Антифрод-система для борьбы с киберпреступностью начала работу в тестовом режиме

evidence.quote: По ее словам, эта единая система свяжет 26 коммерческих банков.
могут заморозить средства потерпевших граждан на 30 дней

summary: Deputy Prosecutor General Umutkan Konkubaeva told a Jogorku Kenesh committee that an anti-fraud system has started in test mode, according to the report. She said the system will link 26 commercial banks; police pass victims' account details to banks, which can freeze funds for 30 days. She said a pilot phase will follow soon.
title: Kyrgyzstan anti-fraud system to link 26 banks starts in test mode, deputy prosecutor general says

validation.note: Only 24.kg read; it relays the deputy prosecutor general's statement to a parliamentary committee.
